survey: nvidia/simready-assets, read on the Jetson AGX Thor

sample.selection_rule: one asset per category, closest to the category's median payload size, categories ordered by how many assets they hold, plus the explicit list; thumbnails excluded

q1_schema.materials: UsdShade Material + Shader + OmniPBR MDL + PNG textures
q1_schema.lod: no LOD prim in any of the 38 sampled packages
two_reader_traps: the geometry is instanced: stage.Traverse() finds 0 meshes; Usd.PrimRange.Stage(stage, Usd.TraverseInstanceProxies()) finds them
the mass is stated twice, on the mesh and on the Xform that wraps it: adding both doubles every asset's mass

what_the_priors_carry: the critic's own six features, measured on the asset's mesh

critic_experiment.answer: No. The SimReady priors do not flag the critic's known-bad prop: the ghost scores 0.149-0.171 against a SimReady-fitted prior, against a threshold of 0.05, and does not separate from the toy mug. Its per-feature percentiles inside the SimReady distribution are 0.14 to 0.94, so the ghost is an ordinary point in the space real objects occupy.

the_other_direction.answer: All 38 real assets score below the critic's own 0.05 ghost threshold against its toy approved set. The mechanism is the fill-ratio feature: it divides a closed mesh's signed volume by the bounding box, real objects are hollow shells (a mug's measured fill ratio is 0.052 against the toy mug's 0.68), and a prior fitted on solid generated meshes calls real objects ghosts.

meshes_not_closed.note: core/genbatch/repair.py welds seams and splits non-manifold edges; on the four sampled assets with the largest defects it reports boundary_edges_closed = 0.

dataset_wide_mass.note: a category is a name, not a scale: warehouse runs from 0.15 kg to 400081 kg, and bodyPart from 0.13 kg to 348 kg

dataset_wide_material_table.hygiene: the material names carry spelling drift (platic, plasic, pastic for plastic; cemaric for ceramic), and one aluminum material carries the plastic density of 950 kg/m3

simready.prop_meaning: every asset in the dataset declares asset_type = prop and profile = Robotics-Prop, including the forklift, the conveyor belt, the structural beam and the 400-tonne warehouse: in SimReady 'prop' means a simulated object, where in builder-ide it means a thing in a room

builder_ide.simready_lite_semantic_slot: an open string with no closed list; the demo uses crate, post, bracket, ground

q3_vocabulary.gap_shape: the unmatched half is the industrial end (handTool 97, consumable 77, serviceTool 57, engineComponent 52, instrument 38, stationery 36, cleaning 29, sign 25, testingTool 25, vehicleSupport 22, powerTool 20): Infinigen builds rooms, SimReady is a workshop
q3_vocabulary.usable_now: the semantic class: SimReady carries a populated taxonomy (Wikidata classes beside human labels and material labels) for a slot builder-ide leaves open

usd_core_on_aarch64.note: 26.11 is the first recent release with an aarch64 wheel; the Thor already carries it in eleven project venvs, so a USD read needs no new install

verification.note: checked with builder-ide's own reader, not the survey's; the first writer put float64 bytes under a float32 accessor and every reader decoded garbage until it was fixed

not_done: textures are not written into the GLB
the sdf and convexDecomposition colliders are not translated into builder-ide's five collision models

joints: joint_door_01_joint_00: revolute about Z, -90 to 0 degrees
joint_door_02_joint_00: revolute about Z, 0 to 90 degrees

drawer_example.joint: joint_slidingJaw_01_joint_00: prismatic along X, -0.045 to 0.055 m
drawer_example.note: searching all 2,677 package names for 'drawer' returns zero assets: the dataset has cabinets with doors, a desk, three shelves and one shelving rack, and no drawer. The bench vise's sliding jaw is the nearest articulated sliding mechanism.

q5_articulation.usable_for_an_agent: partly: the joints are standard UsdPhysics objects with axis, limits and frames, and the three solver variants are already authored as variant sets, so a physics world can instantiate them as they stand; but the joint prims are named from the mesh part, the grasp curve is a curve rather than a named handle, and the sdf collider is not one of builder-ide's five
q5_articulation.not_verified: the glTF path was verified against builder-ide's GLB reader, not against the thor-world viewer, which is a separate repository and is not checked out on this box

cost.budget: 3 GiB for the sample; the director's gate is 5 GiB

box_rules.note: no step came near the 8 GB threshold, so no thor-admit lease was needed; MemAvailable stayed between 69.9 GB and 78.0 GB against a 25.0 GB floor with five other leases running. A thor-admit run invocation for the sample download was refused by the desktop permission gate; the download is network-bound and light on memory.

cost.fetch_method: plain HTTP against the resolve endpoint, one GET per file, driven by the file index; snapshot_download spends an API call per file on a token and hits the anonymous rate limit
